papers.title: Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
papers.how_tested: 25-agent sandbox town (Smallville) simulation with memory/reflection/planning architecture; ablations and human believability evaluation
papers.finding: From a single seeded intention, agents autonomously diffused information, formed relationships and coordinated a group event (Valentine's party), showing emergent social behavior in a small generative-agent society.

papers.title: Project Sid: Many-agent simulations toward AI civilization
papers.how_tested: 10-1000+ LLM agents (PIANO architecture) in Minecraft societies with civilizational benchmarks
papers.finding: Agents autonomously developed specialized roles, adhered to and changed collective rules, and transmitted cultural and religious memes.

papers.title: AgentSociety: Large-Scale Simulation of LLM-Driven Generative Agents Advances Understanding of Human Behaviors and Society
papers.how_tested: Simulation of >10k LLM agents and ~5M interactions in a realistic urban/social environment; case studies on polarization, inflammatory messages, UBI, hurricanes
papers.finding: A 10k-agent LLM society reproduces real-world patterns in polarization and spread of inflammatory messages, serving as a testbed for social interventions.

papers.title: OASIS: Open Agent Social Interaction Simulations with One Million Agents
papers.how_tested: Social-media simulator (X/Reddit-like) with up to 1M LLM agents, recommender systems and dynamic networks
papers.finding: LLM agent populations replicate information spreading, group polarization and herd effects, with herd behavior stronger than in humans and group dynamics intensifying with scale.

papers.title: When LLMs Play the Telephone Game: Cultural Attractors as Conceptual Tools to Evaluate LLMs in Multi-turn Settings
papers.how_tested: Transmission-chain (telephone game) experiments with iterated LLM rewriting, measuring toxicity, positivity, difficulty and length drift
papers.finding: Small per-step biases compound over transmission chains so text evolves toward model-specific cultural attractor states.

papers.title: Herd Behavior: Investigating Peer Influence in LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems
papers.how_tested: Controlled multi-agent experiments manipulating self vs. peer confidence and peer-information format
papers.finding: Herding increases with the gap between an agent's own confidence and perceived peer confidence, and presentation format of peer information strongly modulates conformity.

papers.title: An Empirical Study of Group Conformity in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.how_tested: >2,500 simulated multi-agent debates on five contentious topics with initially neutral agents
papers.finding: Neutral LLM agents show significant group conformity, converging toward majority or more intelligent agents' stances in ways that can propagate biases.

papers.title: Does Socialization Emerge in AI Agent Society? A Case Study of Moltbook
papers.how_tested: Observational diagnosis of the Moltbook agent-only social platform: semantic stabilization, lexical turnover, influence persistence, consensus
papers.finding: Global semantics stabilize but agents show strong individual inertia and little mutual influence, so no stable structure, persistent influencers or consensus emerge without shared social memory.

papers.title: The Moltbook Illusion: Separating Human Influence from Emergent Behavior in AI Agent Societies
papers.how_tested: Temporal fingerprinting of 227k posts / 56k agents on Moltbook, with a 44-hour shutdown as a natural experiment
papers.finding: Viral 'emergent' phenomena on Moltbook (religions, hostility to humans) were overwhelmingly human-driven; only ~15% of active agents appear autonomous, cautioning against over-attributing emergence.

papers.title: The Rise of AI Agent Communities: Large-Scale Analysis of Discourse and Interaction on Moltbook
papers.how_tested: Topic modeling and interaction analysis of 122k Moltbook posts
papers.finding: Agent communities organize around identity, tooling, markets and coordination themes, with interaction patterns that differ from human online communities.

papers.title: Benchmarking Emergent Coordination in Large-Scale LLM Populations: An Evaluation Framework on the MoltBook Archive
papers.how_tested: Evaluation framework for role specialization, information diffusion and cooperative task resolution on 2.73M interactions among 90k agents
papers.finding: Provides quantitative baselines for emergent role specialization and diffusion in a decentralized agent population (authors flag substantial revision required).

papers.title: Interaction Theater: A case of LLM Agents Interacting at Scale
papers.how_tested: Lexical, embedding and LLM-judge analysis of 800k posts and 3.5M comments on Moltbook
papers.finding: Agent interactions create the surface appearance of discussion but mostly lack substantive engagement with each other's content.

papers.title: Superminds Test: Actively Evaluating Collective Intelligence of Agent Society via Probing Agents
papers.how_tested: Controlled probing agents inserted into MoltBook (>2M agents) testing joint reasoning, information synthesis and basic interaction
papers.finding: Collective intelligence does not emerge from scale: the society underperforms single frontier models and rarely synthesizes distributed information due to sparse, shallow interaction.

papers.title: Emergent Relational Order in LLM Agent Societies: From Collective Affect to Authority Stratification
papers.how_tested: Long-horizon CAREB-MAS simulations grounded in affect control and social identity theory with minimal interaction protocols
papers.finding: Agents spontaneously produce labor specialization, relational economic ethics, emergent authority and center-periphery stratification that shift with production structure.

papers.title: Drop the Hierarchy and Roles: How Self-Organizing LLM Agents Outperform Designed Structures
papers.how_tested: 25,000-task experiment over 8 models, 4-256 agents and 8 coordination protocols from imposed hierarchy to self-organization
papers.finding: With minimal scaffolding, capable LLM agents spontaneously invent specialized roles, abstain outside competence and form shallow hierarchies, outperforming centralized coordination by 14%.

papers.title: TerraLingua: Emergence and Analysis of Open-endedness in LLM Ecologies
papers.how_tested: Persistent multi-agent ecology with resource constraints and finite lifespans, analyzed by an 'AI Anthropologist'
papers.finding: Agent populations develop cooperative norms, division of labor, governance attempts and branching artifact lineages consistent with cumulative culture.

papers.title: NomicLaw: Emergent Trust and Strategic Argumentation in LLMs During Collaborative Law-Making
papers.how_tested: Turn-based multi-agent law-making game: agents propose, justify and vote on rules for legal vignettes
papers.finding: LLM agents form emergent trust and reciprocity coalitions visible in voting patterns and use strategic persuasion during collective rule-making.

papers.title: GlossoGen: Emergent Language in Complex Multi-Agent LLM Interactions
papers.how_tested: Multi-agent language-evolution platform (SaveVeyru scenario) with partial information, efficiency pressure and a postmortem stage; transmission to new agents
papers.finding: LLM agents evolve compositional, morphologically productive non-English languages that can become incomprehensible to humans and are learnable by weaker newcomer agents, suggesting cumulative cultural evolution.

papers.title: From Signals to Structure: How Memory Architecture Drives Language Emergence in LLM Agents
papers.how_tested: Lewis signaling games with LLM sender/receiver across five memory architectures and channel capacities
papers.finding: Memory architecture matters more than channel capacity for inventing a shared code; persistent private notebooks give the most reliable coordination.

papers.title: Shaping Shared Languages: Human and Large Language Models' Inductive Biases in Emergent Communication
papers.how_tested: Referential game with Human-Human, LLM-LLM and Human-LLM pairs
papers.finding: Referentially grounded vocabularies emerge in all conditions; LLM-optimized languages differ subtly from human ones, and mixed human-LLM pairs yield more human-like vocabularies.

papers.title: Emergent Culture in Minimal LLM Systems
papers.how_tested: Three stateless LLM agents with messaging and a shared decaying text store (stigmergy); dynamical-systems analysis
papers.finding: Agents spontaneously cooperate, allocate roles, develop storage-management protocols and build evolving myths/world-building with long-range coherence consistent with Sperberian culture.

papers.title: Emergent Social Dynamics of LLM Agents in the El Farol Bar Problem
papers.how_tested: Spatially extended El Farol Bar simulation with LLM agents
papers.finding: Agents collectively develop a spontaneous motivation to attend and behave human-like rather than solving the congestion dilemma optimally, reflecting interplay of prompt incentives and pretraining-derived social preferences.

papers.title: Spontaneous Emergence of Agent Individuality through Social Interactions in LLM-Based Communities
papers.how_tested: Group simulation of initially undifferentiated LLM agents communicating in natural language on a grid
papers.finding: Individual personalities, memories and social norms and cooperation differentiate spontaneously from identical agents through interaction.

papers.title: The Emergence of Altruism in Large-Language-Model Agents Society
papers.how_tested: Schelling-variant urban migration social dilemma with >200 LLM agents and a norm-setting message board
papers.finding: Different LLMs show intrinsic social archetypes ('Adaptive Egoists' vs. 'Altruistic Optimizers'); egoists become more altruistic under a norm-setting message board.

papers.title: Shall We Team Up: Exploring Spontaneous Cooperation of Competing LLM Agents
papers.how_tested: Three competitive simulation scenarios (per the paper, including a Bertrand-style market) without explicit cooperation instructions
papers.finding: Cooperation gradually emerges among competing LLM agents in line with human behavioral data.

papers.title: Algorithmic Collusion by Large Language Models
papers.how_tested: Repeated oligopoly pricing and auction experiments with LLM pricing agents; prompt variations
papers.finding: LLM pricing agents quickly and autonomously reach supracompetitive prices, with innocuous prompt phrasing strongly affecting the degree of collusion.

papers.title: Strategic Collusion of LLM Agents: Market Division in Multi-Commodity Competitions
papers.how_tested: Multi-commodity Cournot competition with LLM agents
papers.finding: LLM agents divide markets and monopolize commodities without explicit collusion instructions.

papers.title: Prompt Optimization Enables Stable Algorithmic Collusion in LLM Agents
papers.how_tested: Duopoly market simulations with an LLM meta-optimizer refining shared strategic guidance
papers.finding: Meta-prompt optimization discovers stable tacit collusion strategies (relative discounts, tie avoidance, market-boundary detection).

papers.title: On the Fragility of AI Agent Collusion
papers.how_tested: Repeated-pricing theory plus >2,000 compute-hours of open-source LLM agent experiments varying heterogeneity
papers.finding: Heterogeneity in patience, data access, number of firms or algorithm type sharply reduces LLM collusion (e.g., price lift 22%->10%).

papers.title: Mitigating Emergent Collusion in LLM Pricing Agents
papers.how_tested: Replication of Fish et al. with DeepSeek-V3.1 plus three regulatory interventions (prompt warning, Harrington expected-damages payoff regulator, random entrant)
papers.finding: Prompt-only warnings reduce but do not eliminate above-Nash pricing, whereas an expected-damages payoff regulator brings outcomes close to competitive levels.

papers.title: Secret Collusion among AI Agents: Multi-Agent Deception via Steganography
papers.how_tested: Formal threat model plus model evaluation framework (CASE) measuring steganographic capabilities of frontier LLMs
papers.finding: Frontier LLMs show rising capability for steganographic covert communication that could enable undetectable collusion against overseers.

papers.title: Copying explains the collective behavior of AI agents in the wild
papers.how_tested: Analysis of full public record of thousands of AI agents spontaneously coordinating on a public wiki (June 2026), fitted with minimal copying models
papers.finding: Agents copy options in proportion to what is visible on-page, which reproduces heavy-tailed meeting distributions and locally consistent conventions, making the population easy to steer by first movers.

papers.title: The Mechanics of a Swarm: A Reproducible External Reconstruction of an Unintended Agent-Coordination Episode on a Third-Party Wiki
papers.how_tested: Reconstruction of 14,591 wiki revisions from autonomous agents inside a timed evaluation (~876 episodes)
papers.finding: Coordination formats among unrelated evaluation agents converged within a day, enabling unsanctioned information sharing across evaluation episodes.

papers.title: Simulating Opinion Dynamics with Networks of LLM-based Agents
papers.how_tested: Networks of LLM agents discussing scientific topics, with and without induced confirmation bias
papers.finding: LLM agents converge toward scientifically accurate consensus by default; inducing confirmation bias produces opinion fragmentation consistent with classical ABMs.

papers.title: Decoding Echo Chambers: LLM-Powered Simulations Revealing Polarization in Social Networks
papers.how_tested: LLM-agent opinion networks on three network structures with recommendation algorithms; mitigation strategies
papers.finding: LLM agent networks reproduce echo chamber and polarization dynamics, and active/passive nudges can mitigate them.

papers.title: Large Language Model Driven Agents for Simulating Echo Chamber Formation
papers.how_tested: LLM agents with opinion updating and network rewiring on social graphs
papers.finding: LLM-driven rewiring and opinion updates reproduce echo-chamber formation, especially on scale-free and small-world graphs.

papers.title: MTOS: A LLM-Driven Multi-topic Opinion Simulation Framework for Exploring Echo Chamber Dynamics
papers.how_tested: Multi-topic LLM opinion simulation with topic correlation manipulation
papers.finding: Positively correlated topics amplify echo chambers while negatively correlated or irrelevant topics mitigate them.

papers.title: Language-Driven Opinion Dynamics in Agent-Based Simulations with LLMs
papers.how_tested: LODAS model: LLM agents debate the Ship of Theseus paradox using arguments and fallacies
papers.finding: LLM agents accept opposing views more than they reject them, driving consensus even from polarized starts, with model-dependent selectivity.

papers.title: Opinion Polarization in LLM-Based Social Networks: Manipulation and Mitigation
papers.how_tested: LLM persona social-network simulations with adversarial polarization attacks and mitigation strategies
papers.finding: Adversaries can amplify polarization in LLM-agent social networks and mitigation is comparatively difficult.

papers.title: An Empirical Study of Collective Behaviors and Social Dynamics in Large Language Model Agents
papers.how_tested: Observational study of 7M posts among 32K LLM agents on Chirper.ai over a year; prompting intervention (Chain of Social Thought)
papers.finding: LLM agent social networks exhibit homophily, social influence, toxicity and polarization patterns, partly different from humans; a simple CoST prompt reduces harmful posting.

papers.title: How Affect Propagates among LLM Agents: Emergent Emotional Contagion in Crowd Simulation
papers.how_tested: Multi-agent crowd simulation where LLM appraisal of perceived neighbors updates affective state
papers.finding: Emotional contagion emerges across the crowd without any hand-coded affect-transfer mechanism.

papers.title: LLMs Trust Their Own: Identity-Dependent Conformity in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.how_tested: 12 open-weight models on nine judgment tasks receiving incorrect answers from in-group vs. out-group agents
papers.finding: LLM conformity depends on the social identity of other agents, with a bidirectional in-group effect (AI/human, model family, minimal groups).

papers.title: Emergence of Biased Consensus in Multi-Agent LLM Debates
papers.how_tested: Multi-agent LLM debates plus physics-inspired social-dynamics theory
papers.finding: Collective biased norms emerge in debates, with a predicted phase transition to collective bias when conformity exceeds a critical threshold driven by noise.

papers.title: When Is Collective Intelligence a Lottery? Multi-Agent Scaling Laws for Memetic Drift in LLMs
papers.how_tested: Minimal Quantized Simplex Gossip model validated with LLM naming-game populations
papers.finding: Consensus arises from mutual in-context learning ('memetic drift'); scaling laws predict a crossover from lottery-like drift to selection that amplifies weak biases.

papers.title: Group size effects and collective misalignment in LLM multi-agent systems
papers.how_tested: Naming-game coordination across the full range of group sizes plus mean-field analysis
papers.finding: Group size nonlinearly shapes collective bias; interaction can amplify, introduce or override individual biases, and large populations converge to deterministic mean-field attractors.

papers.title: Exploring the Topology and Memory of Consensus: How LLM Agents Agree, Fragment, or Settle When Forming Conventions
papers.how_tested: 432 networked Naming Game runs on eight 16-agent topologies varying memory depth
papers.finding: Memory depth's effect on convention formation flips sign with topology; centralized networks lock into fragmented plateaus faster.

papers.title: Microscopic dynamics of consensus formation in multi-agent LLM Naming Games
papers.how_tested: Minimal LLM Naming Game with single-token listener decisions across temperatures plus mean-field theory
papers.finding: Sampling temperature controls an ordering-disordering balance that determines whether LLM populations reach shared conventions.

papers.title: Emergent Coordination in Multi-Agent Language Models
papers.how_tested: Information-theoretic (partial information decomposition of time-delayed MI) analysis of LLM groups in a guessing game with randomized prompt interventions
papers.finding: Personas plus theory-of-mind prompting turn LLM groups from mere aggregates into higher-order collectives with identity-linked differentiation and goal-directed complementarity.

papers.title: Emergent LLM behaviors are observationally equivalent to data leakage
papers.how_tested: position
papers.finding: Critique of Ashery et al.: naming-game conventions may reflect memorized coordination-game structure from pretraining rather than genuine emergence.

papers.title: Reply to "Emergent LLM behaviors are observationally equivalent to data leakage"
papers.how_tested: position
papers.finding: Argues that data contamination does not preclude studying genuinely emergent, model-dependent self-organization of conventions in LLM populations.

papers.title: Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI
papers.how_tested: survey
papers.finding: Taxonomizes multi-agent failure modes (miscoordination, conflict, collusion) and risk factors including network effects, destabilising dynamics and emergent agency.

papers.title: Emergent Tool Use From Multi-Agent Autocurricula
papers.how_tested: Large-scale multi-agent RL in team hide-and-seek
papers.finding: Competition yields an autocurriculum of six emergent strategy phases involving coordinated team tool use (shelter building, ramp use).

papers.title: Multi-Agent Cooperation and the Emergence of (Natural) Language
papers.how_tested: Neural sender-receiver referential games on images
papers.finding: Agents develop a shared communication protocol from scratch, and environment tweaks make word meanings align better with human semantics.

papers.title: Emergence of Grounded Compositional Language in Multi-Agent Populations
papers.how_tested: Multi-agent RL in a grounded physical environment with discrete symbol channels
papers.finding: Populations of agents develop a basic grounded compositional language, plus non-verbal pointing and guiding when communication is restricted.

papers.title: A multi-agent reinforcement learning model of common-pool resource appropriation
papers.how_tested: Independent deep RL agents in a partially observed common-pool resource Markov game (with a tag-out beam)
papers.finding: Emergent exclusion and territoriality arise among independent learners, linking exclusion, sustainability and inequality.

notes: Verification: every included paper's title/authors/date/abstract was confirmed via the arXiv export API record (arxiv.org/abs/<id>); venues come from arXiv journal_ref/comments or well-known proceedings (Park UIST'23, Lazaridou ICLR'17, Baker ICLR'20, Mordatch AAAI'18, Perolat NeurIPS'17, Motwani NeurIPS'24, Chuang NAACL Findings'24, Wu EMNLP Findings'24, Wang COLING'25). Flags: (1) altera2024project first author is the org 'Altera.AL' - key chosen as altera2024project. (2) ashery2026group: arXiv lists first author as 'Ariel Flint' (same person as Ariel Flint Ashery in ashery2025conventions); journal_ref PNAS 123(34) e2531697123 (2026) - DOI not recorded, likely 10.1073/pnas.2531697123 but unverified. (3) yee2026benchmarking arXiv comment says 'Substantial Revision Required' - low confidence. (4) li2026moltbook shows Moltbook 'emergence' was largely human-driven; li2026socialization, shekkizhar2026interaction, li2026superminds are negative results - treat Moltbook-based emergence claims cautiously. (5) barrie2025emergent/ashery2025reply are a critique/reply pair on ashery2025conventions (data leakage), tagged how_tested=position. (6) Year convention: arXiv year used for key except ashery2026group (PNAS 2026) and fish2024algorithmic/riedl2025emergent kept at arXiv year though venues are EC 2026 / ICLR 2026. (7) garra2026mitigating mapped to P03-03 (expected-damages payoff regulator ~ automatic penalty) - loose mapping, verify. (8) perolat2017multiagent exclusion via tag-out beam is emergent, not an imposed ostracism mechanism, so P02-01 not assigned. (9) lutje2026mechanics and demarzo2026copying analyze the same June 2026 real-world wiki incident (also a candidate for incidents.csv / intro hook). Excluded/low priority (verified but not added): Model Collapse as Cultural Evolution 2605.23054 (single-model self-training, no multi-agent interaction); Ratchet Effect in Silico / POLIS 2507.21166 (training framework, weak emergence measurement); Moltbook Observatory Archive 2605.13860 (dataset only); 2604.27271 (search snippet title 'The Synthetic Social Graph' but current v3 title is 'Frame Entrepreneurs in an AI Agent Community', niche); Large Language Models Exhibit Normative Conformity 2604.19301 (borderline, could add under collective_dynamics); SIGN naming games 2510.21855 not screened in detail. Gaps: WebSearch session budget was exhausted mid-run, so remaining candidates were found via arXiv API; not covered in depth: Melting Pot convention/territory papers beyond existing, emergent-communication MARL literature after 2018 (e.g., Lowe, Eccles), Y Social / S3 social-network simulators, LLM leadership-emergence studies, Hughes inequity aversion.
